issues.description: Constructor changes visibility from public to protected without documenting the migration path
issues.detail: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat declares its sole no-arg constructor protected while extending a class that is no longer @Deprecated in the diff. Test-only RW shims typically remain package-private or public for consistency. The invariant 'this class is only for test write paths' should be stated in a class-level comment naming the read-side counterpart.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation removed from legacy formats without explanation
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat lose their @Deprecated marker in this move. The PR description says we should 'prevent users from using the old quantized formats,' yet removing @Deprecated weakens compiler-level signaling. State the invariant: read-only legacy codecs in backward_codecs are still deprecated for new use; reinstate @Deprecated or add a Javadoc rationale.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException with no literate explanation of recovery path
issues.detail: Both formats now throw 'Old codecs may only be used for reading' from fieldsWriter. The message is correct but terse; a careful reader hitting this at runtime needs to know which current format to migrate to (Lucene104HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat per CHANGES.txt). Include the replacement format name in the exception message and the class Javadoc.

issues.description: numMergeWorkers/mergeExec constructor parameters retained but silently discarded
issues.detail: The public multi-arg constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec, validates them, then drops them on the floor since fieldsWriter throws. A caller passing a non-null executor will pass validation, then fail later with a confusing read-only error. Either fail-fast in the constructor for read-only mode or document that these parameters are now inert.

issues.description: Field visibility change from protected to package-private breaks subclass extension
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields move from protected to package-private. This is correct hygiene for a sealed backward-codec, but DenseOffHeapVectorValues remains a public static inner class. If any external code subclassed it (the public constructor suggests this was a supported pattern), the fields become invisible. State the invariant in a class comment: subclassing outside this package is no longer supported.

issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant added without invariant comment
issues.detail: A new package-private constant DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16 appears in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat with no comment on its meaning, why 16, or which reader path consumes it. For a backward-codec being frozen for posterity this is exactly the spot for a literate-programming comment: state what the shift controls, the block size implied (2^16), and which DirectMonotonicReader/Writer pairing depends on it.

review.summary: This is principally a structural move of legacy Lucene99 scalar-quantized formats into backward_codecs, with writers stubbed to throw and visibility tightened. The mechanical refactor looks RIGOROUS in shape, but several literate-programming touches are missing: removed @Deprecated annotations are unexplained, the UnsupportedOperationException doesn't name the replacement codec, and unused constructor parameters silently pass validation. The newly added DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant is exactly the kind of magic number that deserves a one-line invariant comment in code being frozen for backward compatibility. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — correct in algorithm, thin in explanation.
